follow-up time: Until perinatal death or end of the study period (December 2019)
exposure: Lifestyle and habits during early pregnancy
cohort: 44,048 pregnant women in South China recruited between March 2013 and December 2019
finding: Maternal obesity, being employed, history of gestational hypertension, taking antidepressants during early pregnancy, history of gestational diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes mellitus, infertility drug treatment and assisted reproductive techniques, history of neonatal death, preterm birth, and congenital malformations were associated with an increased risk of perinatal death, while ethnic minority, income > 5,000, multiparous women, and cesarean section were associated with a reduced risk.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a reduced risk of perinatal death.
